channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: Lipschitz-Based Robustness Certification Under Floating-Point Execution
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies robustness certification for neural networks and how certified guarantees change when the model runs with floating-point arithmetic instead of exact real arithmetic.
  • Provides counterexamples where robustness certificates based on real-arithmetic assumptions fail under floating-point execution, including adversarially constructed settings.
  • Develops a formal compositional theory and sound conditions that relate Lipschitz/sensitivity bounds to floating-point rounding-error behavior for ReLU feed-forward networks.
  • Implements and empirically evaluates an executable certifier incorporating these floating-point soundness principles.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Toby Murray']
  • Tags: ['robustness certification', 'floating-point semantics', 'Lipschitz/sensitivity bounds', 'adversarial robustness', 'verification']

item.title: Latent Diffusion Inversion Requires Understanding the Latent Space
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies model inversion and membership inference privacy attacks against latent diffusion models (LDMs).
  • Shows LDM memorization is non-uniform across latent codes and latent dimensions, tied to decoder pullback metric geometry.
  • Proposes a method to identify and remove less-memorizing latent dimensions, improving defense against score-based membership inference methods.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Mingxing Rao', 'Bowen Qu', 'Daniel Moyer']
  • Tags: ['Model inversion', 'Membership inference', 'Diffusion models', 'Privacy attacks', 'Latent diffusion (LDM)']

item.title: Principled Steering via Null-space Projection for Jailbreak Defense in Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes NullSteer, a jailbreak defense for vision-language models using null-space projected activation steering to balance safety and utility.
  • Constructs refusal directions that produce no perturbation in the benign activation subspace while inducing refusal on harmful/jailbreak-relevant directions.
  • Claims theoretical justification for preventing safety degradation (avoiding over-refusal) and demonstrates reduced harmful outputs under multiple jailbreak attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Xingyu Zhu', 'Beier Zhu', 'Shuo Wang', 'Junfeng Fang', 'Kesen Zhao', 'Hanwang Zhang', 'Xiangnan He']
  • Tags: ['jailbreak defense', 'activation steering', 'vision-language models', 'robustness', 'safety alignment']

item.title: Natural Adversaries: Fuzzing Autonomous Vehicles with Realistic Roadside Object Placements
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes TrashFuzz, a black-box fuzzing approach that generates realistic adversarial roadside object placements for autonomous vehicles (AVs).
  • Targets AV perception failures by manipulating positions of common roadside objects (e.g., trash bins, billboards, greenery) without using conspicuous or patch-based adversarial artifacts.
  • Enforces realism via constraints based on road/regulatory placement guidelines.
  • Evaluated on Apollo AV system; reports substantial misperceptions and traffic-law violations (15/24).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yang Sun', 'Haoyu Wang', 'Christopher M. Poskitt', 'Jun Sun']
  • Tags: ['adversarial attacks', 'autonomous vehicles', 'black-box fuzzing', 'perception misclassification', 'safety testing']

item.title: Attack Assessment and Augmented Identity Recognition for Human Skeleton Data
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Attack-AAIRS to assess and improve robustness of a skeleton-based person identification model (HCN-ID) against multiple adversarial attack types.
  • Uses GAN-generated synthetic adversarial data learned from a small real dataset to augment training for “inoculation” against unseen attacks.
  • Reports improved robustness to unseen attacks (e.g., FGSM, PGD, MI-FGSM, BIM, Gaussian noise) while maintaining comparable test accuracy on real data.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Joseph G. Zalameda', 'Megan A. Witherow', 'Alexander M. Glandon', 'Jose Aguilera', 'Khan M. Iftekharuddin']
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'adversarial attacks', 'defense via data augmentation/inoculation', 'GAN-generated adversarial examples', 'biometric/person identification']

item.title: Anti-I2V: Safeguarding your photos from malicious image-to-video generation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Anti-I2V, a defense to safeguard photos against malicious image-to-video diffusion generation using person-specific images plus text prompts.
  • Introduces a defense that perturbs diffusion updates beyond RGB, operating in both Lab color space and the frequency domain to improve robustness and target salient pixels.
  • Analyzes denoising network layers to craft training objectives that degrade temporal coherence and generation fidelity of resulting videos.
  • Demonstrates state-of-the-art defense effectiveness across multiple image-to-video diffusion model backbones, including DiT-based architectures.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Duc Vu', 'Anh Nguyen', 'Chi Tran', 'Anh Tran']
  • Tags: ['defense', 'image-to-video diffusion', 'adversarial perturbations', 'temporal coherence', 'privacy/misuse prevention']

item.title: When Understanding Becomes a Risk: Authenticity and Safety Risks in the Emerging Image Generation Paradigm
item.description:
Summary

  • Analyzes safety risks specific to multimodal LLM (MLLM)-based image generation versus diffusion models, focusing on unsafe content generation and fake image synthesis.
  • Finds that MLLMs generate more unsafe images than diffusion models, attributing part of the difference to MLLMs’ ability to interpret abstract prompts rather than failing/corrupting outputs.
  • Evaluates fake image detectors and reports that MLLM-generated images are harder to identify, and that retrained detectors can still be bypassed using longer/more descriptive inputs.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ye Leng', 'Junjie Chu', 'Mingjie Li', 'Chenhao Lin', 'Chao Shen', 'Michael Backes', 'Yun Shen', 'Yang Zhang']
  • Tags: ['MLLM safety', 'Fake image detection', 'Unsafe content generation', 'Adversarial evaluation', 'Benchmarking']

item.title: Leave No Stone Unturned: Uncovering Holistic Audio-Visual Intrinsic Coherence for Deepfake Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes HAVIC, an audio-visual deepfake detector that leverages intrinsic coherence within each modality and across modalities (holistic adaptive fusion).
  • Argues existing detectors underuse joint audio-visual cues and often generalize poorly due to reliance on generator-specific artifacts.
  • Introduces HiFi-AVDF, a dataset of high-fidelity audio-visual forgeries (text-to-video and image-to-video) generated by commercial systems.
  • Evaluates across multiple deepfake benchmarks with strong cross-dataset generalization gains.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jielun Peng', 'Yabin Wang', 'Yaqi Li', 'Long Kong', 'Xiaopeng Hong']
  • Tags: ['deepfake detection', 'audio-visual security', 'multimodal coherence', 'robustness/generalization', 'forgery detection']

item.title: High-Fidelity Face Content Recovery via Tamper-Resilient Versatile Watermarking
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes VeriFi, a tamper-resilient versatile watermarking framework for AIGC/deepfake face images.
  • Targets watermark robustness under strong generative edits using an embedded semantic latent watermark and feature/provenance correlation for localization.
  • Adds high-fidelity content recovery capability to reconstruct original face evidence after manipulations.
  • Introduces an AIGC attack simulator to evaluate robustness against realistic deepfake pipelines.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Peipeng Yu', 'Jinfeng Xie', 'Chengfu Ou', 'Xiaoyu Zhou', 'Jianwei Fei', 'Yunshu Dai', 'Zhihua Xia', 'Chip Hong Chang']
  • Tags: ['AI watermarking', 'Deepfake forensics', 'Robustness to generative edits', 'Content recovery', 'Image security']

item.title: DP^2-VL: Private Photo Dataset Protection by Data Poisoning for Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an identity-affiliation learning privacy threat for vision-language models (VLMs) where attackers fine-tune on a few private photos to embed identity-to-private-property/social relationship associations, enabling leakage via public APIs.
  • Introduces the first identity-affiliation benchmark dataset with multiple identity-centered photo-description scenarios to measure VLM susceptibility.
  • Develops DP2-VL, a dataset protection method that uses data poisoning with imperceptible perturbations to create an embedding-space shift, preventing effective fine-tuning and inducing overfitting on protected data.
  • Reports robustness against post-processing operations and effectiveness across different protection ratios and VLMs (e.g., LLaVA, Qwen-VL, MiniGPT-v2).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hongyi Miao', 'Jun Jia', 'Xincheng Wang', 'Qianli Ma', 'Wei Sun', 'Wangqiu Zhou', 'Dandan Zhu', 'Yewen Cao', 'Zhi Liu', 'Guangtao Zhai']
  • Tags: ['privacy attacks', 'data poisoning', 'vision-language models', 'dataset protection']

item.title: AdvSplat: Adversarial Attacks on Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces AdvSplat, a systematic study of adversarial attacks against feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) models.
  • Uses white-box methods to identify fundamental vulnerabilities, then proposes two query-efficient black-box attack algorithms using frequency-domain parameterizations.
  • Demonstrates that imperceptible pixel-space perturbations to input images can significantly disrupt 3D reconstruction quality across multiple datasets.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yiran Qiao', 'Yiren Lu', 'Yunlai Zhou', 'Rui Yang', 'Linlin Hou', 'Yu Yin', 'Jing Ma']
  • Tags: ['Adversarial Attacks', 'Black-box Attacks', '3D Reconstruction Security', 'Robustness Evaluation', 'Neural Rendering']

item.title: Red-Teaming Vision-Language-Action Models via Quality Diversity Prompt Generation for Robust Robot Policies
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Q-DIG, a red-teaming method that uses Quality Diversity to generate diverse, natural-language instructions that are still task-relevant but induce failures in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) robot policies.
  • Integrates quality-diversity prompt generation with vision-language models to uncover meaningful, varied failure modes caused by instruction wording sensitivity.
  • Evaluates Q-DIG across simulation and real-world settings, showing it finds more diverse failures than baselines; also fine-tunes VLAs on generated adversarial instructions to improve robustness and success on unseen prompts.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Siddharth Srikanth', 'Freddie Liang', 'Ya-Chuan Hsu', 'Varun Bhatt', 'Shihan Zhao', 'Henry Chen', 'Bryon Tjanaka', 'Minjune Hwang', 'Akanksha Saran', 'Daniel Seita', 'Aaquib Tabrez', 'Stefanos Nikolaidis']
  • Tags: ['red-teaming', 'prompt injection-like instruction attacks', 'robustness', 'vision-language-action', 'adversarial instruction generation']

item.title: Alignment Whack-a-Mole : Finetuning Activates Verbatim Recall of Copyrighted Books in Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows that post-training finetuning can bypass existing alignment/safety measures and trigger high-rate verbatim recall of copyrighted books in multiple frontier LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Pro, DeepSeek-V3.1).
  • Uses finetuning on an author/individual style or semantic prompts to extract large verbatim spans (reported up to ~460+ words; 85–90% of held-out books).
  • Demonstrates cross-author generalization and claims the effect reactivates latent memorization from pretraining, with potential security/privacy implications for training-data extraction.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Xinyue Liu', 'Niloofar Mireshghallah', 'Jane C. Ginsburg', 'Tuhin Chakrabarty']
  • Tags: ['model memorization', 'training data extraction', 'privacy/security attacks', 'LLM finetuning vulnerabilities', 'copyrighted content leakage']

item.title: AgentDrift: Unsafe Recommendation Drift Under Tool Corruption Hidden by Ranking Metrics in LLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Examines how LLM agent recommendations drift into unsafe/irrelevant products under corrupted tool outputs while standard ranking metrics (e.g., NDCG) fail to detect it.
  • Introduces a paired-trajectory replay protocol comparing clean vs contaminated tool-output conditions across multiple dialogue steps and LLMs.
  • Finds a consistent evaluation-blindness: utility/recommendation quality appears preserved, yet safety violations occur in 65–93% of turns, often driven by information-channel corruption early in the trajectory.
  • Proposes a safety-penalized metric variant (sNDCG) and argues for trajectory-level safety monitoring rather than single-turn quality evaluation.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zekun Wu', 'Adriano Koshiyama', 'Sahan Bulathwela', 'Maria Perez-Ortiz']
  • Tags: ['tool-output corruption', 'LLM agents', 'evaluation metrics', 'adversarial robustness', 'trajectory-level safety']

item.title: ChartAttack: Testing the Vulnerability of LLMs to Malicious Prompting in Chart Generation
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces ChartAttack to test multimodal LLM vulnerability to malicious prompting in chart generation by injecting misleading elements into chart designs.
  • Proposes AttackViz dataset of chart spec + QA pairs labeled with effective misleaders and incorrect induced answers.
  • Shows significant degradation in chart QA accuracy (17.2 points in-domain, 11.9 points cross-domain) and suggests fine-tuning for robustness against misleading charts.
  • Emphasizes need for security/robustness in deployment of LLM-based chart generation systems.

Paper Type

  • Research/Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jesus-German Ortiz-Barajas', 'Jonathan Tonglet', 'Vivek Gupta', 'Iryna Gurevych']
  • Tags: ['prompt injection/malicious prompting', 'multimodal LLMs', 'chart/visual misinformation', 'robustness evaluation', 'attack dataset/benchmark']

item.title: Analysing the Safety Pitfalls of Steering Vectors
item.description:
Summary

  • Performs a systematic safety audit of activation steering via Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA).
  • Finds that steering vectors can substantially increase or decrease jailbreak attack success rates across multiple LLM families and sizes.
  • Uses JailbreakBench under a unified protocol to quantify how steering amplifies safety vulnerabilities (up to +57% ASR) or mitigates them (down to -50% ASR).
  • Attributes the safety gap to overlap between steering directions and latent refusal behavior directions.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yuxiao Li', 'Alina Fastowski', 'Efstratios Zaradoukas', 'Bardh Prenkaj', 'Gjergji Kasneci']
  • Tags: ['jailbreaking', 'activation steering', 'LLM safety', 'red teaming', 'attack evaluation']

item.title: How Vulnerable Are Edge LLMs?
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies security risk of quantized LLMs on edge devices, focusing on query-based knowledge extraction (model stealing/behavioral recovery).
  • Shows quantization adds noise but does not prevent recovery of underlying semantic knowledge under realistic query budgets.
  • Introduces CLIQ (Clustered Instruction Querying) to construct structured queries that improve semantic coverage and reduce redundancy to enable more efficient extraction.
  • Experiments on quantized Qwen models (INT8/INT4) demonstrate that CLIQ substantially improves extraction effectiveness under limited budgets.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ao Ding', 'Hongzong Li', 'Zi Liang', 'Zhanpeng Shi', 'Shuxin Zhuang', 'Shiqin Tang', 'Rong Feng', 'Ping Lu']
  • Tags: ['model extraction', 'knowledge extraction', 'prompt/query attacks', 'quantized/edge LLM security', 'LLM security evaluation']

item.title: Internal Safety Collapse in Frontier Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Identifies a failure mode in frontier LLMs called Internal Safety Collapse (ISC) where models generate harmful content while performing otherwise benign tasks under specific conditions.
  • Proposes the TVD (Task, Validator, Data) framework to trigger ISC and introduces ISC-Bench with 53 scenarios across 8 professional disciplines.
  • Reports very high worst-case safety failure rates (avg 95.3%) on jailbreak-related evaluation across multiple frontier LLMs, claiming ISC can exceed standard jailbreak attacks.
  • Concludes that alignment may change surface behavior but does not remove underlying unsafe capabilities, increasing dual-use risk in real deployments.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yutao Wu', 'Xiao Liu', 'Yifeng Gao', 'Xiang Zheng', 'Hanxun Huang', 'Yige Li', 'Cong Wang', 'Bo Li', 'Xingjun Ma', 'Yu-Gang Jiang']
  • Tags: ['LLM safety', 'Jailbreaks/Adversarial behavior', 'Benchmarking', 'Safety evaluation', 'Internal failure modes']

item.title: Toward a Multi-Layer ML-Based Security Framework for Industrial IoT
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a multi-layer ML-based security framework for Industrial IoT (IIoT) using trust models/architectures and ML to predict/mitigate degraded network conditions affecting trust convergence.
  • Claims improved trust convergence time while maintaining robustness against adversarial behaviors.
  • Includes a deployment architecture using low-cost open-source hardware and outlines ongoing work toward multi-layer attack detection (including physical-layer threats) and robustness against adversarial ML attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research/Thesis Framework (doctoral thesis overview)

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Aymen Bouferroum (FUN)', 'Valeria Loscri (FUN)', 'Abderrahim Benslimane (LIA)']
  • Tags: ['IIoT security', 'ML-based trust/security framework', 'attack detection', 'adversarial robustness', 'multi-layer security']

item.title: Claudini: Autoresearch Discovers State-of-the-Art Adversarial Attack Algorithms for LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents Claudini, an autoresearch-style LLM-agent pipeline that automatically discovers new white-box adversarial attack algorithms for LLMs.
  • Demonstrates improved jailbreaking and prompt-injection attack performance over 30+ existing methods, including higher attack success rates on evaluated safeguards.
  • Shows transferability of attacks optimized on surrogate models to held-out models (cross-model generalization).
  • Releases discovered attacks and evaluation code/implementations via the referenced GitHub repository.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Alexander Panfilov', 'Peter Romov', 'Igor Shilov', 'Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye', 'Jonas Geiping', 'Maksym Andriushchenko']
  • Tags: ['LLM security', 'Jailbreaking', 'Prompt injection', 'Adversarial attacks', 'Autoresearch/automated red teaming']

item.title: Uncovering Memorization in Timeseries Imputation models: LBRM Membership Inference and its link to attribute Leakage
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a two-stage privacy attack framework for time series imputation models: membership inference and attribute inference.
  • Membership inference uses a reference-model approach to improve black-box detection accuracy, including against overfitting-based robustness.
  • Introduces an attribute inference attack to predict sensitive characteristics of training data for time series imputation.
  • Empirically demonstrates substantially higher retrieval/precision than baselines across attention-based and autoencoder architectures, including fine-tuning scenarios with partial adversary knowledge.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Faiz Taleb', 'Ivan Gazeau', 'Maryline Laurent']
  • Tags: ['privacy attacks', 'membership inference', 'attribute inference', 'time series imputation', 'black-box inference']

item.title: Likelihood hacking in probabilistic program synthesis
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies an RL training-time vulnerability in probabilistic program synthesis where models exploit the reward by generating programs with invalid/unnormalized distributions (failure likelihood hacking).
  • Formalizes the likelihood-hacking (LH) behavior in a probabilistic programming language and derives syntactic conditions to prevent it.
  • Presents a defense via a restricted “safe” language fragment and an implemented LH-resistant variant of Stan (SafeStan), with empirical results showing reduced violation rates.
  • Evaluates the vulnerability by observing GRPO-trained models quickly finding LH exploits during training.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jacek Karwowski', 'Younesse Kaddar', 'Zihuiwen Ye', 'Nikolay Malkin', 'Sam Staton']
  • Tags: ['AI security vulnerabilities', 'reward hacking', 'probabilistic program synthesis', 'RL safety constraints', 'Bayesian model discovery']

item.title: Why the Maximum Second Derivative of Activations Matters for Adversarial Robustness
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies how activation function curvature (max |σ''|) affects adversarial robustness.
  • Finds a non-monotonic/U-shaped trade-off: too little curvature reduces expressivity, while too much curvature leads to sharper minima that hurt robust generalization.
  • Provides theoretical explanation via effects on the Hessian diagonal of the loss and validates experimentally across architectures/datasets and adversarial training methods.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yunrui Yu', 'Hang Su', 'Jun Zhu']
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'adversarial examples', 'model training/regularization', 'theoretical analysis', 'neural network activations']

item.title: PoiCGAN: A Targeted Poisoning Based on Feature-Label Joint Perturbation in Federated Learning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes PoiCGAN, a targeted data poisoning attack for federated learning using feature-label joint perturbations via a conditional GAN.
  • Designed to evade defenses that rely on model anomaly detection by maintaining high stealthiness and keeping main-task accuracy close to baseline.
  • Implements an ideal poison generator that can produce targeted poisoned samples and perform label flipping during training.
  • Experiments report significantly higher attack success rate with limited accuracy degradation.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Tao Liu', 'Jiguang Lv', 'Dapeng Man', 'Weiye Xi', 'Yaole Li', 'Feiyu Zhao', 'Kuiming Wang', 'Yingchao Bian', 'Chen Xu', 'Wu Yang']
  • Tags: ['data poisoning', 'federated learning', 'targeted attacks', 'adversarial/stealthy poisoning', 'label flipping']

item.title: Mind Your HEARTBEAT! Claw Background Execution Inherently Enables Silent Memory Pollution
item.description:
Summary

  • Identifies a security vulnerability in Claw personal AI agents where untrusted content processed during heartbeat-driven background execution can silently pollute agent memory.
  • Shows an Exposure → Memory → Behavior pathway: background-ingested misinformation can be written to long-term memory and later influence user-facing behavior without user awareness or provenance.
  • Provides empirical instantiation via MissClaw, demonstrating high rates of misleading short-term influence (up to 61%) and long-term memory pollution (up to 91%), with cross-session behavioral effects up to 76%.
  • Finds that social credibility/consensus cues drive short-term influence and that the issue persists under naturalistic browsing with context pruning; no prompt injection is required.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yechao Zhang', 'Shiqian Zhao', 'Jie Zhang', 'Gelei Deng', 'Jiawen Zhang', 'Xiaogeng Liu', 'Chaowei Xiao', 'Tianwei Zhang']
  • Tags: ['AI security vulnerability', 'prompt injection (not required)', 'memory pollution', 'agent background execution', 'privacy/model integrity']

item.title: DeepXplain: XAI-Guided Autonomous Defense Against Multi-Stage APT Campaigns
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes DeepXplain, an explainable deep reinforcement learning framework for defending against multi-stage APT (Advanced Persistent Threat) cyber campaigns.
  • Uses provenance-based graph learning and temporal stage estimation to recognize and adapt to attack stages.
  • Incorporates explanation signals into the DRL policy optimization via evidence alignment and confidence-aware reward shaping (not purely post-hoc explanations).
  • Evaluated in a realistic enterprise testbed with reported gains in detection/defense success and explanation metrics (confidence/fidelity).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Trung V. Phan', 'Thomas Bauschert']
  • Tags: ['APT defense', 'Explainable reinforcement learning', 'Cyber attack detection', 'Provenance graph learning', 'Stage-aware temporal modeling']

item.title: Agent Control Protocol: Admission Control for Agent Actions
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Agent Control Protocol (ACP), a cryptographic admission-control layer that mediates autonomous agent actions before state execution.
  • Uses identity/capability-based authorization with delegation chains, transitive revocation, deterministic risk evaluation, and cryptographically chained auditing.
  • Includes adversarial evaluation claiming active evasion attempts are blocked and per-agent isolation is maintained under coordinated multi-agent testing.

Paper Type

  • Research/Specification

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Marcelo Fernandez (TraslaIA)']
  • Tags: ['agent security', 'admission control', 'cryptographic authorization', 'adversarial evaluation', 'autonomous systems governance']

item.description:

item.title: Anti-I2V: Safeguarding your photos from malicious image-to-video generation
item.description:

  • Analyzes denoising network layers to craft training objectives that degrade temporal coherence and generation fidelity of resulting videos.

item.title: Invisible Threats from Model Context Protocol: Generating Stealthy Injection Payload via Tree-based Adaptive Search
item.description:

item.title: The Cognitive Firewall:Securing Browser Based AI Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Via Hybrid Edge Cloud Defense
item.description:
Summary

item.title: Internal Safety Collapse in Frontier Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary
